title: Titer (Serial Dilution Endpoint)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

expression: Titer = 1 / (highest dilution showing a positive endpoint)
explanation: Expresses the concentration of an antibody, antigen, virus, or other agent as the reciprocal of the greatest dilution of the original sample that still produces a detectable positive result in a serial dilution assay (e.g. agglutination, plaque formation, or another endpoint readout). A higher titer means the sample remained positive at a higher dilution, indicating a greater original concentration of the agent being measured.

variables.symbol: highest dilution showing a positive endpoint
variables.meaning: The most dilute sample in the series that still gives a positive/detectable result, expressed as a dilution factor (e.g. 1:128)

workedExample.scenario: A two-fold serial dilution series (1:2, 1:4, 1:8 ... 1:256) of a serum sample remains positive through the 1:128 dilution but is negative at 1:256.
workedExample.substitution: Titer expressed as the reciprocal of 1:128

commonMistakes: Reporting the last dilution tested rather than the last dilution that was actually positive.
Comparing titers from assays run on different days/plates/reagent lots as if they were directly comparable without accounting for inter-assay variation.
Ignoring that titer values from a two-fold series can only take specific discrete values, so small true differences may not be resolvable.
